title: Herto Homo sapiens fossils
summary: Excavations at Herto in Ethiopia's Middle Awash recovered three crania, two adult and one child, dated by argon-argon methods to 160,000-154,000 years ago. Described in 2003 as Homo sapiens idaltu, they were among the oldest well-dated anatomically modern human fossils then known and showed signs of post-mortem treatment.

as_recorded.value: Radioisotopically dated to between 160,000 and 154,000 years ago
Sediments and volcanic rock dated to 160,000-154,000 years; site found 16 November 1997

where.modern_name: Herto, Bouri Formation, Middle Awash, Afar region, Ethiopia
where.historical_name: Lake-margin landscape in the Afar depression, no polity

importance.justification: Well-dated African fossils from the 100,000-300,000-year gap that support an African origin for modern humans.

sources.title: Pleistocene Homo sapiens from Middle Awash, Ethiopia (Nature 423:742-747; copy hosted by in-africa.org)

reviewer_note: Coordinates are the differentially corrected GPS point of holotype locality BOU-VP 16 (10 deg 15.5484 min N, 40 deg 33.3834 min E) in White et al. 2003. The Berkeley item is a press release (class reference). Whether the subspecies name idaltu is still accepted was not checked.
